title: An Exhibition Designed for Its Next Venue
transcript:
A travelling science exhibition is changing the way its display structures are built. Instead of designing a unique set of walls and cases for each venue, the organisers have created a collection of reusable sections. The change began when staff reviewed what happened to exhibition materials after the public had gone home.

At several venues, carefully constructed displays had been dismantled into pieces that were difficult to reuse. A panel designed to fit one particular room could not easily be adapted elsewhere. Transporting reusable materials also created a challenge: bulky structures occupied space in vehicles even when their weight was relatively low.

The new system uses sections that can be separated and packed flat. Their surfaces can accept different graphics, while the supporting frames remain the same. Designers initially worried that this would make every exhibition look identical. A trial showed that varied arrangements and lighting could create distinct experiences without replacing the basic structure.

The organisers are now measuring more than the amount of material saved at each venue. They record the number of journeys, the time needed for assembly and the repairs required after repeated use. One early design used a particularly light component, but it was damaged so frequently that replacement and repair outweighed the advantage of carrying less weight. A slightly heavier alternative proved more useful over several moves.

The exhibition director says that the project has shifted attention from a single opening night to the full life of the display. A structure should be judged by how it performs through packing, transport, assembly and reuse. The current system will not suit every building or object, but it gives future hosts a starting point that does not assume everything must be built from scratch.

questions.prompt: What prompted the organisers to redesign the exhibition structures?
options: Visitors had requested fewer scientific displays.
Materials were often difficult to reuse after an exhibition closed.
Every venue had exactly the same floor plan.
Transport companies refused to carry any wooden panels.
questions.answer: Materials were often difficult to reuse after an exhibition closed.
questions.explanation: 回顾发现大量为特定场地制作的展板拆除后难以再次利用。

questions.prompt: How does the new system reduce the need to replace entire displays?
options: It keeps the same graphics at every venue permanently.
It removes all supporting frames from the exhibition.
Reusable frames can carry different graphics and be rearranged.
It requires each host to construct additional walls.
questions.answer: Reusable frames can carry different graphics and be rearranged.
questions.explanation: 基本框架保留，可更换图文并通过布局和灯光形成不同体验。

questions.prompt: Why was the particularly light component replaced?
options: Frequent damage made its repair and replacement outweigh the transport benefit.
It could not be separated from the building’s original walls.
Visitors could not see the graphics attached to it.
It was heavier than every alternative considered.
questions.answer: Frequent damage made its repair and replacement outweigh the transport benefit.
questions.explanation: 轻型部件过于容易损坏，维修替换负担抵消了减轻运输重量的优势。

questions.prompt: What change in thinking does the director emphasise?
options: Judging displays only by how they look on opening night.
Using the same layout regardless of the building.
Avoiding all repairs once materials have been reused.
Evaluating a display through its full cycle of transport, assembly and reuse.
questions.answer: Evaluating a display through its full cycle of transport, assembly and reuse.
questions.explanation: 设计评价应覆盖打包、运输、组装及重复使用的全生命周期。
